newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU opens full probe into Boeing, McDonnell merger.
newsitem.headline: EU opens full probe into Boeing, McDonnell merger.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it was starting a full probe into the proposed alliance between Boeing Co and Mcdonnell-Douglas Corp.
The widely expected move is aimed at assessing to what extent Boeing, already the world's largest aircraft maker, would increase its dominance of the civil aviation market.

"The Commission will, in particular, have to examine to what extent Boeing's leading position in the market for commercial jet aircraft could be strengthened by the proposed merger," the Commission said in a statement.

The EU's competition watchdog said it was also concerned that the alliance with McDonnell would give Boeing greater access to the space and defence business, thus strengthening its power over aircraft equipment suppliers.

"The Commission will...need to investigate to what extent the large increase in Boeing's defence and space business could strengthen its market position in commercial aircraft, for example in terms of overall financial resources, greater access to technology developed in the defence and space sector, and increased bargaining power vis-a-vis equipment suppliers," the statement said.

Boeing chairman and chief executive officer Phil Condit said last week in Brussels, where he met European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert, that he was expecting the alliance to clear all regulatory hurdles by July.
The deal, which consists in Boeing taking over ailing McDonnell, is also being investigated by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission.
Under EU merger rules, which ban creation or strengthening of dominant positions in the 15-nation bloc, the Commission has a maximum of four months to come to a final decision.

It has the power to investigate corporate mergers and takeovers involving companies with a combined worldwide turnover of five billion European currency units and European sales of at least 250 million Ecus each. This also applies to deals involving only non-EU companies.
Boeing has 60 percent of the world's market for commercial airliners of more than 100 seats, the Commission said.

It noted that the deal would represent "a further increase in Boeing's market share" leaving only one competitor: the European Airbus consortium between Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace, Aerospatiale of France, British Aerospace and Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas.
The Commission also pointed out that the merger will lead to a large increase in Boeing's defence and space business.

"Without taking into account the recently completed acquisition of Rockwell Defence and Aerospace, Boeing will approximately triple its defence and space activities through the merger with McDonnell Douglas", the statement read.

Condit argued last week that the acquisition of McDonnell would not alter the current market situation much, because the firm was no longer "a significant player". Last year Boeing also swallowed the defence and aerospace units of Rockwell International Corp.
